key_insight: The paper finds that standard on-policy distillation breaks when the student makes mistakes because the teacher can recognize errors but still fails to recover from them. CriticOPD fixes this by adding critique-based supervision, restoring the teacher’s ability to guide the student back to correct solutions.
problem_solved: It addresses the unreliability of supervision in on-policy distillation when training on the student’s own rollouts. The core challenge is that a teacher may not be recoverable from incorrect prefixes, which weakens training signal and harms learning.
method: Use the student’s own generated rollouts as training trajectories, as in on-policy distillation.
Have the teacher explicitly critique incorrect rollouts instead of only following them token by token.
Convert critiques into supervision signals that help the teacher recover to the correct answer path, improving training stability and correctness.
impact: This makes on-policy distillation more reliable on hard or error-prone trajectories, which can improve student learning from imperfect self-generated data. For practitioners, it offers a practical way to get stronger supervision without needing perfectly correct rollouts.

paper_title: Recovering Reliable Supervision via Critique-Guided On-Policy Distillation
paper_authors: Kaixiang Zhao, Tianrun Yu, Shangzhe Li, Yuxiao Yang, Amanda Hughes
